name: nextjs-tailwind-v4-build-fixes
content:
--- name: nextjs-tailwind-v4-build-fixes description: | Diagnose and fix Next.js + Tailwind v4 build failures caused by PostCSS parsing errors in generated CSS. Covers the Tailwind v4 arbitrary-value parser bug for `bg-[var(--…)]` / `bg-[image:var(--…)]` (PostCSS emits corrupted rules with control characters), the Next.js dev cache staleness issue (stale errors persist after source fixes until `.build/next` + `.next` are wiped), the static-CSS-class fallback pattern in `globals.css`, the theme-token replacement for `accent-[var(--…)]`, and the verification ladder. Trigger when dev server returns 500 on every route, when logs show `Parsing CSS source code failed` at line numbers far higher than your globals.css file length, when arbitrary-value utilities with `var(--color-…)` produce escaped control chars in generated CSS, or when fixing source files has no effect because the dev server is replaying old errors. category: software-development --- # Next.js + Tailwind v4 Build Fixes ## When to use - Dev server (`npm run dev`) returns **500 on every route** including `/login` and `/`. - Dev log shows: `Parsing CSS source code failed … ./src/app/globals.css:NNN:NN` where the offending line number is far higher than the actual file length — that number refers to Tailwind's *generated* CSS, not your source. Verify with `wc -l src/app/globals.css` (e.g. file is 506 lines but error says line 6179 → generated CSS). - Generated CSS contains **escaped control characters** like `\b`, `\u0015`, `\u{14}`, `\u{35b}` inside what should be `var(--…)`. This is the Tailwind v4 PostCSS extractor mangling `--name` lookups in arbitrary values. - You fixed every `bg-[var(--…)]` source occurrence but the error keeps recurring → stale Next.js dev cache. - `accent-[var(--color-primary)]` in markup produces `accent-color: var(--color-primary)` in CSS but the parser fails. Use the theme token (`accent-primary`) instead. ## Tailwind v4 PostCSS bug pattern When you write any of these in markup: ```tsx
…
…
…
…
``` Tailwind v4's source extractor reads them, generates CSS rules like: ```css .bg-\[var\(--color-surface\)\] { background-color: var(--color-surface); } ``` …but in some configurations the extractor **mangles** the `--` inside the arbitrary value, producing: ```css .bg-\[var\(-�\u{14}or-su\b �\)\] { background-color: var(-�\u{14}or-su\b �); } ``` The PostCSS CSS parser then chokes on `var(-�)` because `-` followed by a non-identifier char is invalid syntax. The whole generated stylesheet fails to parse, every route 500s. This is reproducible and intermittent — same project can survive a clean rebuild or hit it again on next edit. When it hits, the static-CSS-class fallback below is the durable fix. ## Fix patterns ### 1. Static CSS class in globals.css (preferred for gradients) For brand-specific gradients / multi-property var-backed backgrounds, declare a static utility class in `src/app/globals.css` next to other custom utilities (`bg-hero-gradient`, `bg-vibrancy`): ```css /* Brand gradient — avoids Tailwind v4 PostCSS bug for bg-[image:var(--…)] */ .bg-grad-brand { background-image: var(--grad-brand); } ``` Then use it as a normal class: ```tsx ``` ### 2. Theme token for color utilities For arbitrary `accent-[var(--color-primary)]`, `text-[var(--color-…)]`, `border-[var(--color-…)]` — register the var as a `@theme` color in globals.css and use the token: ```css @theme { --color-primary: #E54D5E; --color-accent-light: #F47C5E; } ``` ```tsx
``` Tailwind generates clean `.accent-primary { accent-color: var(--color-primary); }` rules that parse correctly. ### 3. Literal hex / arbitrary property value (when var lookup is unnecessary) If the value never needs to change (e.g. forbidden page chrome, static dashboard chrome): ```tsx // Before (PostCSS-unsafe)
// After (literal hex — works, but loses dark-mode CSS-var indirection)
``` Use this only for values that genuinely don't change with theme. For dark-mode-aware surfaces, prefer the static-class fallback. ## Diagnostic ladder ```bash # 1. Confirm the dev server is actually running on the expected port lsof -i :20128 2>/dev/null | head -5 curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'login %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:20128/login # 2. Find the offending arbitrary-value classes in YOUR source grep -rn 'bg-\[var(--\|bg-\[image:var(--\|text-\[var(--\|accent-\[var(--' src/ # 3. If grep returns nothing but the error persists → stale cache wc -l src/app/globals.css # If the error's line number >> your file's line count, it's generated CSS # 4. Wipe BOTH Next caches and restart kill -9 rm -rf .next .build/next/dev .build/next/cache npm run dev ``` ## Stale cache — the trap that wastes hours A Next.js dev server caches compiled CSS chunks in **two** places: - `./.next` (Next.js cache) - `./.build/next/dev` (the project's compiled chunks, including `.build/next/dev/static/chunks/src_app_globals_css_*.single.css`) After you patch a `.tsx` file that referenced `bg-[var(--…)]` and the dev server still emits the same `Parsing CSS source code failed …:6179:27` error: 1. The source has been fixed. 2. The generated CSS in `.build/next/dev/static/chunks/*.single.css` is stale. 3. Even on a fresh restart, Next can re-read the stale chunk and replay the old compile error in the log, masking the new good state. **Always wipe both**: `rm -rf .next .build/next/dev` (or `.build/next` for full paranoia). Restart the server. Then curl `/login` to verify a 200, not a 500. ## Verification ```bash # After fix + cache wipe, all of these should return 200 or 307 (redirect): for path in /login / /forbidden /dashboard /dashboard/logs /dashboard/usage; do code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 4 "http://localhost:20128$path") echo "$path: $code" done # And the dev log should have zero "Parsing CSS source code failed" entries: tail -500 .build/next/dev/logs/next-development.log | grep -c "Parsing CSS" # Expected: 0 ``` If grep -c returns >0, the cache wasn't fully wiped or there's still a source file you missed — re-run the diagnostic ladder. ## Pitfalls 1. **`bg-[var(--…)]` is NOT safe in Tailwind v4** — even with a fallback value (`#fff`) — the parser still mangles the `--` token. Treat it as a known broken pattern, not a stylistic preference. 2. **`bg-[image:var(--…)]` is also broken** — different code path inside the extractor, same end result. Same fix. 3. **Grep across file extensions only finds the obvious cases** — `*.css`, `*.tsx`, `*.ts`, `*.jsx`, `*.js`, `*.mdx` cover source. CSS chunks under `.build/next/dev/static/chunks/*.single.css` are generated artifacts; do NOT edit them. 4. **The error line number is GENERATED CSS line** — `globals.css:6179` doesn't mean your source has a problem at line 6179. It means Tailwind emitted line 6179 in its in-memory output that fails to round-trip through PostCSS. Use the column hint (`27` is almost always `--` mangling inside `var(`) to recognise the pattern. 5. **Don't trust a single grep** — `grep -rln 'bg-\\[var('` may miss cases where the class string is built at runtime (`cn(...)`) or split across a JS template literal. If the error persists after a clean cache wipe, look for runtime string concatenation that produces `bg-[var(--…)]`. 6. **`accent-[var(--…)]`** — same parser, same fix: use the theme token `accent-` instead. 7. **The Next.js dev server caches PostCSS compile output aggressively** — patches that should fix the issue look broken until you nuke `.next` AND `.build/next`. Don't chase phantom source bugs in already-clean files. 8. **Phantom errors from killed background `npm run dev` procs** — when the user re-runs the dev script while one is already running, the second invocation collides, prints `⨯ Another next dev server is already running. PID: …` then closes. Its `tee /tmp/last_dev.log` will have *overwritten* the previous log file with that error transcript. Before assuming the live server is broken, verify it's actually serving 200s: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:/login` and check `lsof -iTCP: -sTCP:LISTEN`. The killed proc's log output is NOT the current state. 9. **Stale `.build/next/dev/logs/next-development.log` can still contain `Parsing CSS` entries from hours ago** — `grep -c "Parsing CSS" .../next-development.log` will return >0 forever unless the log file is rotated. Always cross-check with `curl` to a real route and with the latest tail of `tee /tmp/last_dev.log` before declaring a regression. 10. **`tee` clobbers on each invocation** — scripts that pipe `npm run dev 2>&1 | tee /tmp/last_dev.log` overwrite the log file completely. If the new dev-server attempt fails fast (port collision, etc.), `tee` writes only that failure transcript and you lose the prior healthy log. Either append (`tee -a`) or read `next-development.log` directly for the canonical record. 11. **Wipe `.next/server` too, not just cache/build** — for full paranoia after a CSS or PostCSS-corruption error, the project used a three-directory wipe: `.next/cache`, `.next/build`, `.next/server`. (For omniroute specifically with `distDir = .build/next`, the equivalent is `.build/next/dev` + `.build/next/cache` + `.build/next/server` — but in practice `.build/next/dev/static/chunks/*.single.css` is the only one that matters.) ## Quick triage order when the user reports "dev server is broken" 1. **Don't read the log first.** `curl /login` and check the HTTP code. 2. **If 200/307**, the live server is fine — the user is likely looking at a stale log file or a log from a killed background process. Confirm by tailing the *current* `tee`'d output file (if any) and the running PID's log under `.build/next/dev/logs/next-development.log`. Tell them the server is healthy. 3. **If 500**, then read the log. Locate the `Parsing CSS source code failed` block, identify the column hint (27 = `--` mangling), grep the source for the arbitrary-value pattern, patch, then do the dual-directory wipe. 4. **If multiple `npm run dev` processes are visible** in `pgrep -f 'run-next\|next dev'` or `lsof -iTCP:`, kill all but the lowest PID. Re-curl. ## References - `references/omniroute-session-evidence.md` — Full session transcript for the omniroute fix (branch `release/v3.8.49`, port 20128): exact error transcripts from `next-development.log`, the four files actually patched, and the verification commands that proved the cache wipe + restart produced 200/307 responses across all routes. Use this when you need a worked example to pattern-match against.

# omniroute — Tailwind v4 PostCSS Bug Evidence

Session that produced this skill: `omniroute` repo, branch `release/v3.8.49`, dev server on port 20128.

## Symptoms observed

- `/login`, `/`, `/dashboard/*` all returned **HTTP 500** immediately after replacing theme-token classes with arbitrary `bg-[var(--…)]` utilities as part of a wider cleanup.
- Dev log (`/Users/0x/Desktop/omniroute/.build/next/dev/logs/next-development.log`) emitted these recurring errors:

```
[Server] ERROR [browser] "./src/app/globals.css:6179:27
Parsing CSS source code failed
  6177 |   }
  6178 |   .bg-\[image\:var\(-\\15 ��-brand\)\] {
> 6179 |     background-image: var(-\\u0015��-brand);
       |                           ^
  6180 |   }
  6181 |   .from-\[\\#E54D5E\] {
  6182 |     --tw-gradient-from: #E54D5E;

Unexpected token Delim('-')
```

…and three more variants for `bg-[var(--color-surface)]`, `accent-[var(--color-primary)]`, and a corrupted `p-[var(--color-surface)]` from another file that had been patched but still emitted the broken rule.

## Diagnostic moves

1. `grep -rln '\[var(--' src/` — found 4 source files; patched all of them.
2. Dev server still 500. Restarted. Still 500.
3. Checked actual error line in `globals.css`: `wc -l` returned 506. Error was on line 6179 → Tailwind's generated CSS, not the source.
4. Realized Next had cached the PostCSS output in `.build/next/dev/static/chunks/src_app_globals_css_*.single.css`.
5. `kill -9 <pid>; rm -rf .next .build/next/dev; npm run dev` → `/login` returned 200.

## Files actually patched in this session

- `src/shared/components/Button.tsx` — primary variant class: `bg-[image:var(--grad-brand)]` → `bg-grad-brand`
- `src/app/globals.css` — added `.bg-grad-brand { background-image: var(--grad-brand); }` next to existing `.bg-hero-gradient` and `.bg-vibrancy` utilities.
- `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/usage/components/ProviderLimits/ProviderUsdCostModal.tsx` — `accent-[var(--color-primary,#E54D5E)]` → `accent-primary` (theme token via `@theme { --color-primary: #E54D5E }` in globals.css).
- `src/app/forbidden/page.tsx` — two `bg-[var(...)]` and `text-[var(...)]` classes replaced with literal hex (`bg-[#0a0a0f]`, `text-[#e0e0e0]`, `text-[#888]`).
- `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/logs/page.tsx` — 4 occurrences of `bg-[var(--card-bg,#1e1e2e)]`, `border-[var(--border,#333)]`, `text-[var(--text-secondary,#aaa)]`, `hover:bg-[var(--hover-bg,#2a2a3e)]` replaced with literal hex equivalents.

## Why literal hex was chosen for forbidden/page.tsx and logs/page.tsx

These two pages use one-off brand chrome that doesn't respond to dark-mode theme switching. Adding a theme token for each var (`--bg-primary`, `--card-bg`, `--border`, `--text-secondary`, `--hover-bg`, `--accent`) would have widened the `@theme` block for two pages that don't benefit from the indirection. Hex is the pragmatic call here — the static-CSS-class fallback is reserved for cases where dark-mode support matters (gradients, surface tones).

## Verification commands that proved the fix

```bash
# After cache wipe + restart:
for path in /login / /forbidden /dashboard /dashboard/logs /dashboard/usage; do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 4 "http://localhost:20128$path")
  echo "$path: $code"
done
# /login: 200, /: 307, /forbidden: 200, /dashboard: 307, /dashboard/logs: 307, /dashboard/usage: 307

tail -100 /tmp/last_dev.log | grep -c "Parsing CSS"
# 0
```

## Lesson crystallized

The `.next` cache wipe alone is **not enough** when `distDir = .build/next` is configured (as in omniroute). Both directories must be cleared, and both `next` processes must be killed before restarting, otherwise the second process inherits the first's compiled-but-broken PostCSS state.
